{{Short description|American mathematician and politician}}
'''Stephanie Frank Singer''' (born 1964) is an American mathematician and politician in [[Philadelphia]], [[Pennsylvania]]. Singer was a professor at [[Haverford College]] from 1991 to 2002 before founding Campaign Scientific, a computer data business for political organizations. She was elected as a [[Philadelphia City Commissioner]] in November 2011.

==Early life and education==
Singer was born in 1964 to [[Maxine Singer|Maxine]] and Daniel Singer.<ref name="married" /><ref>{{cite web |title=Libraries Catalog: Stephanie Singer |url=https://catalog.library.tamu.edu/Author/Home?author=Singer%2C+Stephanie+Frank%2C+1964- |publisher=Texas A&M University Libraries |access-date=June 9, 2024 |language=en}}</ref> Her mother was a [[molecular biologist]] and her father was an attorney for [[Fried, Frank, Harris, Shriver & Jacobson]].<ref name="married" />

Singer graduated from [[Yale University]] and earned a Ph.D. in 1991 at [[New York University]].<ref name="married" /><ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=33605}}</ref> She spent a year in graduate studies at [[Stanford University]] for computer science.<ref name="tech" />

==Career==
=== Academic ===
Singer was a professor at [[Haverford College]] from 1991 to 2002, where she earned tenure. She experienced [[sexual harassment]] while at the school, which she discussed in a 2017 article in ''[[The Chronicle of Higher Education]]''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.chronicle.com/article/I-Spoke-Up-Against-My-Harasser/241991|title=I Spoke Up Against My Harasser — and Paid a Steep Price|access-date=2020-01-17|website=[[The Chronicle of Higher Education]]}}</ref>

She founded Campaign Scientific, which provided data services to political organizations and businesses.<ref name="whyyi">{{cite news |title=Philadelphia elections with Commissioner Stephanie Singer |url=https://whyy.org/episodes/philadelphia-elections-with-commissioner-stephanie-singer-2/ |work=[[WHYY-TV|WHYY]] |date=May 8, 2012}}</ref> In 2002, she began requesting data from the [[Philadelphia City Commissioners|Office of the Philadelphia Commissioners]], which is responsible for conducting elections in the city, to post the data on an unofficial website for the city's Democratic party.<ref name="tech">{{cite news |last1=Reyes |first1=Juliana |title=Analyze the Vote: Use this web app to visualize City of Philadelphia election data |url=https://technical.ly/uncategorized/analyze-the-vote-use-this-web-app-to-visualize-city-of-philadelphia-election-data/ |work=Technical.ly |date=July 18, 2012 |language=en}}</ref> The commission would only provide data in paper form until Singer threatened to sue them in 2008.<ref name="tech" />

=== Politics ===
Singer became increasingly active in politics after volunteering to work on election data for the [[John Kerry 2004 presidential campaign|2004 presidential campaign]] of [[John Kerry]].<ref name="removal" /> In 2008, she was elected [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic Party]] committeeperson for Philadelphia's 8th Ward, an influential position representing [[Center City, Philadelphia|Center City]].<ref name="phim">{{cite news |last1=Kerkstra |first1=Patrick |title=City Commissioners Al Schmidt and Stephanie Singer Just Can't Get Along |url=https://www.phillymag.com/news/2013/03/29/city-commissioners-al-schmidt-stephanie-singer/ |work=[[Philadelphia Magazine]] |date=March 29, 2013}}</ref>

In 2011, she was elected as a [[Philadelphia City Commissioner]], defeating 36-year incumbent [[Marge Tartaglione]].  She ran an aggressive campaign, describing her opponent as "an embarrassment".<ref>{{cite news |last1=Warner |first1=Bob |title=Marge looking at end of her city reign? |url=https://www.inquirer.com/philly/news/politics/20110517_Marge_looking_at_end_of_her_city_reign_.html |work=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]] |date=May 17, 2011 |language=en}}</ref> Her campaign was endorsed by the ''[[Philadelphia Daily News]]'' and [[Johnny Dougherty|John Dougherty]] and his IBEW Local 98.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Gibson |first1=Keegan |title=Preview: Philly City Commission |url=https://www.politicspa.com/preview-philly-city-commission/24335/ |work=PoliticsPA |date=May 17, 2011}}</ref> She was sworn into office on January 3, 2012.<ref name="whyyi" /> During her time in office, she clashed with the other commissioners, [[U.S. Republican Party|Republican]] [[Al Schmidt]] and Democrat Anthony Clark, as well as the chair of the Philadelphia Democratic Party, [[U.S. Representative]] [[Bob Brady]].<ref name="sigs">{{cite news |last1=Brennan |first1=Chris |title=Singer comes up short for city commissioner ballot |url=https://www.inquirer.com/philly/blogs/heardinthehall/Singer-comes-up-short-for-city-commissioner-ballot.html |work=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]] |date=March 27, 2015 |language=en}}</ref> The day after the city's handling of the November 6, 2012 elections led to criticism of the commission, Schmidt and Clark voted to remove Singer as chair of the commissioner and appoint themselves as co-chairs.<ref name="removal">{{cite news |last1=Warner |first1=Bob |title=Philadelphia's city commissioners oust Singer as chair |url=https://www.inquirer.com/philly/news/politics/20121107_Philadelphias_city_commissioners_oust_Singer_as_chair.html |work=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]] |date=November 7, 2012 |language=en}}</ref> ''[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]]'' reported that the removal did not appear related to the election, however, and noted that the commissioners "had been bickering for months at their weekly public sessions over seemingly small issues" as well as Singer's vocal opposition to the state's new [[Voter identification laws in the United States#Registration and election day voter ID laws by state|voter ID law]].<ref name="removal" /> Prior to their election, Singer and Schmidt had both run as progressive reformers, and Schmidt had initially voted with Singer to appoint her chair.<ref name="phim" /><ref>{{cite news |last1=Warner |first1=Bob |title=After election disarray, Philadelphia City Commissioners try to regroup |url=https://www.inquirer.com/philly/news/politics/20121126_After_election_disarray__Philadelphia_City_Commissioners_try_to_regroup.html |work=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]] |date=November 26, 2012 |language=en}}</ref>

Singer's reelection attempt in 2015 was challenged by three Democratic voters for failing to obtain the required 1,000 signatures on nomination petitions, falling four short.<ref name="sigs" /> In March 2015, Common Pleas Court Judge Joel Johnson removed her from the Democratic primary ballot.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Otterbein |first1=Holly |title=City Commissioner Stephanie Singer Gets A Chance To Fight for Her Political Life |url=https://www.phillymag.com/citified/2015/03/31/city-commissioner-stephanie-singer-fight-for-life/ |work=[[Philadelphia Magazine]] |date=March 31, 2015}}</ref> Her term as city commissioner ended in 2016.<ref>{{citation|title=Biography of Commissioner Stephanie Singer|url=http://www.philadelphiavotes.com/en/about-us/commissioner-stephanie-singer|archive-url=https://archive.today/20150415182813/http://www.philadelphiavotes.com/en/about-us/commissioner-stephanie-singer|publisher=Office of the Philadelphia City Commissioners|access-date=2015-12-10|archive-date=2015-04-15|url-status=dead}}.</ref>

In October 2018, Singer launched a [[podcast]] entitled ''Defend Democracy!'' where she reflects on her experience as a former election official, data strategist, and successful candidate, with advice to those who have interests in entering politics.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://anchor.fm/stephanie-frank-singer|title=Defend Democracy! • A podcast on Anchor|website=Anchor|language=en|access-date=2019-01-16}}</ref>

==Personal life==
She is the daughter of [[Molecular biology|molecular biologist]] and science administrator [[Maxine Singer]] and the sister of historian [[Amy Singer (historian)|Amy Singer]].

Singer married Stephen Fischer in 1993 in a ceremony officiated by [[Ruth Bader Ginsburg]], then a judge for the [[United States Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit]].<ref name="married">{{cite news |title=Weddings: Stephanie Singer, Stephen Fischer |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1993/05/31/style/weddings-stephanie-singer-stephen-fischer.html |work=The New York Times |date=May 31, 1993}}</ref>
